description:
## Goal

Protect the subscription-first Tauri listener lifecycle added by PR #55 (`bsm-wj1.1`) with deterministic React StrictMode regression tests. The completed feature must prove that stale StrictMode setup work cleans itself up, the live setup alone retains listeners, startup reads happen exactly once, and a real unmount cannot reactivate pending asynchronous registrations.

This is test coverage for behavior that is already correct. Do not change production listener behavior unless a child task first reproduces a separate defect.

**Triage:** ready-for-agent

## Project context

Beadsmith presents the Issue List as a live view of the Current Workspace. ADR-0007 (`docs/adr/0007-refresh-issue-list-by-polling-beadwork-ref.md:21-42`) defines a backend poller that emits full Issue List snapshots through Tauri after `refs/heads/beadwork` moves. The renderer registers two listeners:

- `workspace-transition`, which owns Current Workspace changes;
- `beadwork://issue-explorer-state-changed`, which updates the Issue List within the current Workspace selection.

PR #55 made startup subscription-first: `App` must await both listener registrations before it dispatches the initial Issue snapshot and Workspace-state reads. This prevents the renderer from missing an early refresh event during startup.

## Relevant code

Line numbers refer to `main` at merge commit `b1ea93b3` and may drift.

- `src/main.tsx:16-18` enables `React.StrictMode`.
- `src/lib/use-external-lifecycle.ts:23-37` wraps `useEffect`; each effect setup calls the supplied `effect()` callback.
- `src/App.tsx:181-274` owns listener registration, startup dispatch, and cleanup.
- `src/App.tsx:182` declares the closure-local `let disposed = false`.
- `src/App.tsx:192-216` registers transition then refresh, sequentially.
- `src/App.tsx:199-203` and `211-215` store live unlisteners or immediately invoke late stale unlisteners.
- `src/App.tsx:218-250` defines startup Issue and Workspace reads.
- `src/App.tsx:252-268` waits for registration and suppresses startup after disposal.
- `src/App.tsx:270-274` marks that setup disposed and removes handles already received.
- `src/lib/UseExternalLifecycle.test.tsx` has dependency lifecycle tests but no StrictMode/deferred-work proof.
- `src/test/app-workspace-fixtures.ts:39-74` has an immediate listener mock, which is insufficient for controlled interleavings.
- `src/App.issue-refresh.test.tsx:18-120` shows the current App/TauRPC/Tauri mocking boundary.

## Investigation result and design intent

A review alleged that cleanup from StrictMode setup 1 could set setup 2's `disposed` flag, leaving duplicate listeners or suppressing startup. That claim is incorrect because each invocation of the lifecycle callback creates a new JavaScript lexical environment:

```text
setup 1 creates disposed_1 = false
cleanup 1 sets disposed_1 = true
setup 2 creates disposed_2 = false
```

The bindings are different variables. IIFE 1 captures only `disposed_1`; IIFE 2 captures only `disposed_2`. After StrictMode's development-only setup → cleanup → setup cycle, late run-1 registrations observe `disposed_1 === true` and immediately unlisten. Run 1 skips startup. Run-2 registrations observe `disposed_2 === false`, remain active, and dispatch startup once.

Do not replace this with `useRef<boolean>`. A shared ref reset to `false` by setup 2 would also appear false to stale IIFE 1, allowing it to retain handles after cleanup 1 has already run. That would create the duplicate-listener/startup race the review incorrectly attributed to the current closure-local code. A shared solution would require generation tokens, but no shared state is needed here.

## Feature invariants

The child tasks collectively must leave executable proof that:

1. StrictMode setups have separate local disposal state.
2. A late registration from a disposed setup immediately unregisters.
3. Cleanup from one setup cannot remove or retain another setup's listeners.
4. Startup waits for both listeners owned by the live setup.
5. StrictMode dispatches the initial Issue load and `workspace_state()` exactly once.
6. Unmounting while registrations are pending prevents every late handle from becoming live.
7. Unmounting after registration removes each live listener exactly once.

## Test strategy

Use the real `App` rendered inside `React.StrictMode`. Mock Tauri's `listen()` with manually controlled promises and one unlisten spy per logical registration:

- `T1`: stale setup's transition registration;
- `R1`: stale setup's refresh registration;
- `T2`: live setup's transition registration;
- `R2`: live setup's refresh registration.

Within each setup, transition must resolve before App requests refresh. Tests must use `act` or the equivalent Testing Library boundary, not sleeps or timers. Prefer a focused `src/App.strict-mode-lifecycle.test.tsx`; keep the existing immediate helper simple unless a deferred helper is genuinely reusable.

## Scope

In scope: test-only helpers, StrictMode setup/cleanup behavior, listener completion ordering, exactly-once startup, and real unmount cleanup.

Out of scope: Rust refresh coordination, transition-gate rules, event contracts, WebDriver tests, broad Workspace audits, replacing the local flag, or treating Tauri's generic registration-to-unlisten transport window as a reproduced defect.

## Child tasks and sequencing

- `bsm-wj1.5.1` — prove `useExternalLifecycle` setup-local state under StrictMode. This edits the hook test and can proceed independently.
- `bsm-wj1.5.2` — build the deferred App listener harness and add stale-first coverage.
- `bsm-wj1.5.3` — add the live-first ordering that directly answers the original review claim; depends on `.2`.
- `bsm-wj1.5.4` — extend the two edge cases to all six valid completion orders; depends on `.3`.
- `bsm-wj1.5.5` — cover real unmount while registrations are pending; depends on `.4` so the focused suite has one writer/merge sequence.
- `bsm-wj1.5.6` — cover real unmount after registration reaches steady state; depends on `.5`.

```mermaid
graph LR
  A[bsm-wj1.5.1 Hook StrictMode proof]
  B[bsm-wj1.5.2 Stale-first + harness] --> C[bsm-wj1.5.3 Live-first]
  C --> D[bsm-wj1.5.4 Six-order matrix]
  D --> E[bsm-wj1.5.5 Pending unmount]
  E --> F[bsm-wj1.5.6 Steady-state unmount]
```

The App tasks are deliberately serialized because they are expected to edit the same focused test file and build on one harness. The hook task is independent because it targets `src/lib/UseExternalLifecycle.test.tsx`.

## Feature completion

This feature is complete when all child tasks are closed and the following pass:

```sh
pnpm exec vitest run src/lib/UseExternalLifecycle.test.tsx src/App.strict-mode-lifecycle.test.tsx src/App.issue-refresh.test.tsx src/App.workspace-switching.test.tsx src/App.workspace-recovery.test.tsx
pnpm test
pnpm check
pnpm doctor
```

Substitute the actual focused test filename if needed. No Rust or desktop E2E command is required unless production code changes.
title: Add StrictMode regression coverage for App listener lifecycle
